transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
President Trump is polling the nomination of Dr. Heidi Overton to lead the FDA.
The move comes after growing signs that Overton did not have the votes needed to win Senate
confirmation.
She faced questions from the top Republican on the Senate health committee and others
about her approach to vaccines.
After she backed a controversial proposal to break up combination shots for children,
it was ahead of a key vote on her nomination, which is set for tomorrow.
President Trump is in Manila for a regional summit and next heads to Shenzhen, China for
more high-stakes meetings.
NPR's Deepa Shiveram reports.
Analysts say it's significant that Trump met with U.S. allies like India, Japan and Australia
before he heads to China for meetings with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir
Putin.
The president emphasized the importance of alliances with democracies in the Pacific region
and he signed a trade deal with Thailand.
The next stop for Trump is Shenzhen, the high-tech city that neighbors Hong Kong.
It's where she is hosting a large economic summit.
This is Trump's first trip abroad since his party lost control of the next Congress.
Trump's priorities with allies and adversaries, including discussions on the Iran war and
Russia's war in Ukraine, are being closely watched.
Deepa Shiveram, NPR News, Shenzhen.
Trump House Democrat Hakeem Jeffries of New York called for a briefing of intelligence
leaders on Capitol Hill after a series of high-profile tech outages in the last week.
NPR's Eric McDaniel has this report.
Jeffries, so far the only declared candidate for Speaker of the House and the new Congress,
says that after flights went down and tech behemoths faltered, disrupting huge swaths
of the U.S. economy, it's time for some information from the Trump administration.
I think it's time for the administration to come up to the Hill and explain themselves
so we can be informed about the steps that need to be taken and we can inform the people
of the United States of America.
So far the administration has not given any suggestions that the outage is the result
of malignant actors, Eric McDaniel and PR News Washington.
Invidia is trying to move past the scandal involving its now former CEO Jensen Huang's
extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged spy.
The company's board chair says it will not reinstate Huang, as Ricky Mulvey from NPR's
The Indicator from Planet Money tells us Invidia's business has been going gangbusters for a
while now and that remains true.
Revenue is about $116 billion for the quarter.
That's about double from a year ago, beating expectations.
And the biggest financial story other than the scandal is that this quarter Invidia started
shipping their new AI supercomputers, ones that can help scientists look into black holes
or develop the latest and greatest large language models.
That is, according to Interim CEO Collette Kress, off to an explosive start.
Look, Invidia is an extraordinarily profitable business on the bleeding edge of technology.
That doesn't fundamentally change with this scandal.
NPR's Ricky Mulvey reporting the U.S. stock market dropped again today.
This is NPR News from Washington.
Congress has agreed to require civilian aircraft to carry systems that help pilots locate nearby
planes.
Lawmakers have been crafting a compromise bill addressing 50 recommendations from the
National Transportation Safety Board.
It comes after 67 people were killed in a collision between an American Airlines flight
and an Army Black Hawk helicopter near Washington, D.C., last year.
Waymo has temporarily stopped freeway operations of its driverless cars nationwide after the
California DMV restricted the company's freeway use over safety concerns.
From member station KQED, Azul Daulstrom Ekman reports.
The order's been in effect since last week.
The California DMV says Waymo's freeway operations posed a "imminent hazard" to public safety.
That's after several recent incidents, including one where three Waymo robo-taxis entered an
active construction closure on a freeway in the San Francisco Bay Area.
In a statement, Waymo said it halted freeway operations in other markets, like in Phoenix
Arizona and Los Angeles, while its vehicles continue to operate on surface streets.
The DMV's order will be in place until Waymo provides evidence that it's corrected the
issue.
For NPR News, I'm Azul Daulstrom Ekman in San Francisco.
The Cambridge dictionary has chosen "human" as its word of the year.
The choice highlights the debate over how AI blurs the lines between machines and people.
The dictionary's lexicographer notes that AI is changing how we talk about being human.
The word human has been in use since the 1450s and is defined as having qualities, faults,
and feelings that people have.
This is NPR.

Trump in Manila for regional summit, then heads to Shenzhen, China for high-stakes meetings
Hakeem Jeffries calls for intelligence leaders briefing after series of high-profile tech outages
Nvidia moves past scandal involving former CEO Jensen Huang's extramarital affairs; quarterly revenue doubles
Congress agrees to require civilian aircraft to carry systems that help pilots locate nearby planes
